source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: The unit of appraisal is a research programme, not a single theory. A programme has a hard core, a protective belt of auxiliary hypotheses, and a heuristic (a problem-solving machinery).
numbers: Newtonian hard core = 4 statements (three laws of mechanics + law of gravitation).
quote: All theories, in this sense, are born refuted and die refuted.
limits: Lakatos admits his sketches are caricature ('some statements are to be taken not with a grain, but with tons, of salt').
agent_relevance: Separate the few commitments held fixed (core) from the many revisable patches (belt) and track the pair as a series, not one answer.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Negative heuristic: forbid modus tollens against the hard core; redirect a failed prediction onto the auxiliary belt. The belt bears the brunt of tests and may be adjusted or replaced.
numbers: Rule is a methodological decision by proponents, not a logical fact.
quote: A research programme is successful if all this leads to a progressive problemshift; unsuccessful if it leads to a degenerating problemshift.
limits: Core is irrefutable by decision only; Lakatos says the core may crumble when the programme stops anticipating novel facts.
agent_relevance: Direct model of handling a failed check: patch assumptions or setup first, protect commitments, but keep a score of what the patches bought.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Positive heuristic: a partly articulated plan of ever more complex models. The scientist follows the plan and mostly ignores anomalies in the early models. Refutations of early models are expected.
numbers: Newton sequence: fixed point sun + one point planet; both orbit common centre; several planets with no interplanetary force; mass balls; spinning balls; interplanetary forces and perturbations; bulging planets. Early changes were driven by theory difficulty, not data. The maths delayed the Principia by more than a decade.
quote: Nothing shows the existence of a positive heuristic of a research programme clearer than this fact: this is why one speaks of 'models'.
limits: Hindsight reconstruction; Lakatos says Newton must have been fully aware of the falsity of early variants, which is not documented.
agent_relevance: Supports a planned ladder of model refinements rather than reactive patching; early failures of a simple model are not by themselves a stop signal.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Core definition of progress: a series of theories is theoretically progressive if each new one has excess empirical content over its predecessor (predicts novel facts). It is empirically progressive if some of that excess content is corroborated. Degenerating otherwise.
numbers: Two clauses: excess content (checked instantly by logic) and some excess content verified (may take an indefinite time).
limits: Content comparison is hard for real theories; Lakatos gives no measure.
agent_relevance: Gives a counted signal: per patch, did it add checkable predictions (clause 1) and did any survive a test (clause 2). Both can be coded in a scaffold.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Formal falsification rule: T is falsified only when a rival T' exists that (1) has excess empirical content, (2) explains all of T's unrefuted earlier success, and (3) has some excess content corroborated.
numbers: Three conditions, all required.
quote: there is no refutation without a better theory.
limits: Needs a rival to be present. A lone degenerating programme is never forced out by this rule alone.
agent_relevance: Do not drop a working answer plan on one failed check without a candidate alternative that covers what the first got right (cf. G2, G3).

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Intermittent progress is enough. Each step must be content-increasing, but only every now and then must content be seen to be corroborated. Long runs of failed tests are rationally tolerable.
numbers: No count of steps or years given. Examples: Prout programme ran from 1815 to about 1911; Halley's comet return came 72 years after the prediction.
quote: We do not demand that each step produce immediately an observed new fact.
limits: Open ended: no threshold for how long is too long. This is the core weakness for a stopping rule.
agent_relevance: The agent needs its own explicit patience budget (patches without a new corroborated prediction), because Lakatos supplies none.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Degenerating programme: theories are fabricated only to accommodate known facts; the theory lags behind the facts and runs fast to catch up. Marxism is Lakatos's example.
numbers: Four failed bold predictions listed: absolute impoverishment of workers; first revolution in most industrial society; no revolutions in socialist societies; no conflicts of interest between socialist countries. Post-hoc patches: theory of imperialism, and explanations of Berlin 1953, Budapest 1956, Prague 1968, Russia-China split.
quote: their auxiliary hypotheses were all cooked up after the event to protect Marxian theory from the facts.
limits: Political example and a contested historical judgement; the Urbach/IQ case (a20) shows a verdict that later flipped.
agent_relevance: Pattern for the impasse detector: a patch cooked up after the failure that predicts nothing else is the degenerating signature.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Progress is marked by novel, surprising predictions, not by trivial confirmations. A few stunning ones tip the balance.
numbers: Newton: Halley predicted a comet return in 72 years to the minute; Newtonians predicted small planets. Einstein: star separation differs between night and during an eclipse. Rival views of comets then: divine warnings; Kepler's straight-line motion.
quote: Nobody had thought to make such an observation before Einstein's programme.
limits: Novelty is theory-relative and can take long to see (see Balmer case, a13).
agent_relevance: Weight corroborated novel predictions far above confirmation of what the agent already knew; require a held-out check (aligns with G3).

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: There is no instant rationality. Budding programmes need lenient treatment, programmes may take decades to become empirically progressive, and crucial experiments are recognised as crucial only decades later.
numbers: Kepler's ellipses admitted as crucial for Newton against Descartes about 100 years later. Mercury's perihelion anomaly known for decades, a refutation only once Einstein explained it. Young's 1802 double-slit accepted only after Fresnel developed wave optics. Brownian motion unresolved for nearly a century.
quote: The methodology of scientific research programmes does not offer instant rationality.
limits: Cuts against any fast stop rule: hindsight judgement cannot be used online without extra assumptions.
agent_relevance: Warns against a hard stop on a single signal; an impasse detector should be a flag with a cost, not a verdict.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Appraisal is not advice. It is rational to stay with a degenerating programme and try to make it progressive. What is irrational is to deny its poor public record.
numbers: Practical rule: journals should decline papers that only reassert or absorb counter-evidence by ad hoc adjustment; funders should withhold money.
quote: It is perfectly rational to play a risky game: what is irrational is to deceive oneself about the risk.
limits: Feyerabend and Kuhn charge that this leaves no usable guidance; Lakatos answers by separating appraisal from heuristic advice.
agent_relevance: Maps to G1/G6: the agent may continue a risky line but must keep an honest ledger of its record and report it.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Prout case: a programme progressing in an ocean of anomalies. Prout (1815) claimed atomic weights are whole numbers; anomalies were blamed on impure samples, so the programme attacked the observational theories (purification methods).
numbers: Stas in 1860 declared the theory without foundations; Marignac replied the deviations could stem from impurity; Crookes 1886 proposed fractionation; resolved about a century later via isotopes (Rutherford school). Chlorine weight 35.5 was the refutation.
quote: Prout's theory defeated the theories previously applied in purification of chemical substances one after the other.
limits: Lakatos says this is rational reconstruction: Prout himself denied anomalies. Crookes's own patches predicted nothing new and were dropped.
agent_relevance: A failed check may reflect a faulty measurement theory. Check the test's own assumptions before patching the core; such a patch is legitimate only if content-increasing.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Bohr case, degenerating phase: the 1913 Bohr programme was progressive. Later it was swamped by anomalies and ever more ad hoc hypotheses, then replaced by wave mechanics (de Broglie 1924, then the Davisson-Germer experiment).
numbers: Bohr's five postulates are the core. Spin and relativistic splitting were handled by ad hoc steps (1924). Wave mechanics predicted a new fact (Davisson-Germer) and explained the ad hoc later theories.
quote: With ever more sterile inconsistencies and ever more ad hoc hypotheses, the degenerating phase of the research programme had set in.
limits: Lakatos concedes the timing was coincidence: de Broglie in 1914 instead of 1924 would change the story. Nunan 1982 published an immanent criticism (a29, metadata only).
agent_relevance: Archetype of degeneration: more patches, each fitting a known fact, no new fact; a rival then explains old successes plus a new one. Use as a labelled pattern for the S6 detector.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Novelty is not a simple property. The Balmer formula was known before Bohr, but Bohr's theory implied a different statement (energy-level differences obey it), so Lakatos counts it as novel, and novelty may take long to judge.
numbers: Three levels: B1 hydrogen lines obey Balmer; B2 energy-level differences obey it; B0 lines from tubes in specified conditions obey it.
quote: the novelty of a factual proposition can frequently be seen only after a long period has elapsed.
limits: Seed of the later split into temporal, use- and theory-relative novelty (Zahar, Worrall); the text does not settle it.
agent_relevance: Define novel by what the patch was fitted to. A held-out fact not used when building the patch is the operational version.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Degrees of ad hoc. Ad hoc1: no excess content. Ad hoc2: excess content but none corroborated. Ad hoc3: heuristically unmotivated (defined in the 1968 paper and footnotes).
numbers: Bohr-Kramers-Slater 1924 had excess content, but all its new predictions were refuted. Fitzgerald contraction was ad hoc2, not ad hoc1 (Lakatos corrects Popper).
limits: Definitions sit mostly in footnotes citing the 1968 paper; ad hoc3 not read in full here.
agent_relevance: Three-way tag for patches: no new content / new content untested / new content refuted. Only the second keeps patience; the third counts against the programme.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Duhem and Quine are the ancestors. Lakatos rejects Duhem's vague good sense and simplicity as taste and fashion, and replaces them with an explicit content test on the series of adjustments.
numbers: Duhem lets a core crumble for aesthetic reasons; Lakatos wants logical and empirical reasons.
quote: Why not rather impose certain standards on the theoretical adjustments by which one is allowed to save a theory?
limits: Duhem-Quine holism means a single failed test is ambiguous about where the error lies.
agent_relevance: A failed check does not say which assumption failed; locate the fault with real output (G2) before choosing what to patch.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Pluralism beats monism. Competition between programmes should start early; objective elimination of a programme comes only from a rival that explains its success and outruns it.
numbers: Lakatos: Popper and Feyerabend are right and Kuhn is wrong on pluralism.
quote: a degenerating problemshift is no more a sufficient reason to eliminate a research programme than some old-fashioned 'refutation' or a Kuhnian 'crisis'.
limits: Needs a rival programme to exist, which a single agent may lack.
agent_relevance: Keep at least two live hypotheses in the search states; a stop signal for one should trigger search for a rival, not just abandonment.

source: Lakatos (1970/1978) Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, in The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes, Cambridge UP (full text via pdftotext of archive.org scan)
finding: Lakatos concedes there is no predictable saturation point: no limit on human imagination in inventing content-increasing theories, and even false theories can win empirical successes.
numbers: Footnote revises his own 1963-64 Hegelian view that programmes have a saturation point.
limits: Means the when-to-stop question is open inside his own framework.
agent_relevance: A stopping rule must be an external budget; the theory will not give one.

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Imre Lakatos
finding: Summary of MSRP. Progressive = theoretically and empirically progressive; degenerating if not. Both are degrees and can reverse, so a degenerating programme can recover.
numbers: Novelty is comparative: a prediction counts only if neither rivals nor conventional wisdom predict it.
limits: First 100000 of 130627 characters read, then the Feyerabend section.
agent_relevance: Recovery is possible, so a stop signal should be revisable.

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Imre Lakatos (Feyerabend section)
finding: Feyerabend's dilemma: applied rigorously, MSRP condemns degenerating programmes that may later recover (excluding good science, as Lakatos charged Popper); if only appraisal not advice, it is close to anything goes.
numbers: Lakatos left no developed reply in surviving letters; the author calls it still an open problem.
limits: Single-author reading.
agent_relevance: Central tension for our guardrail: a degenerating flag cannot be a hard stop. It should be a cost-bearing prompt to switch strategy.

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Imre Lakatos (Urbach/IQ case)
finding: Lakatosian verdicts have reversed. Urbach judged the environmentalist IQ programme degenerating; the Flynn effect later undid that.
numbers: One reversal; no counts given.
limits: SEP calls it an own goal; detail only summarised in the page text I read.
agent_relevance: Concrete failure of early degeneration calls: keep the stop rule soft and re-testable.

source: Wikipedia: Imre Lakatos (MSRP summary)
finding: Critique: Lakatos never showed scientists actually switched when his criterion was met (he admitted this in 1968). Feyerabend: any development satisfies the progressiveness demand, so the demand does not restrict practice.
numbers: Lakatos died 2 Feb 1974. Dates: 1968 paper, 1970 volume chapter, 1973 lectures, 1975 conference, 1978 collection.
limits: Encyclopedia summary only; Cronin 1991 Darwin dispute not read.
agent_relevance: The criterion may be too loose; a counted rule is needed to give it bite.

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Scientific Progress
finding: Laudan's alternative: effectiveness = importance-weighted solved empirical problems minus anomalies and conceptual problems. An anomaly is a problem unsolved by the theory but solved by a rival.
numbers: Formula is comparative. Critics: problems hard to individuate (Mars's orbit as one problem or infinitely many); Bird: accumulating false solutions counts as progress.
limits: Laudan's weights are unspecified.
agent_relevance: A ledger of solved vs unsolved sub-problems is a direct computational analogue; the individuation problem warns against counting trivial sub-problems.

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Pseudo-Science and the Demarcation Problem
finding: Lakatos's criterion would call a field pseudoscientific if non-progressive even when practitioners try to improve it (unlike Thagard). Popper attacks Kuhn's puzzle-solving criterion because astrologers also solve puzzles.
numbers: Quote: theories fabricated only in order to accommodate known facts.
limits: Laudan's 'Demise of the Demarcation Problem' only cited, not summarised.
agent_relevance: Use the degenerating label per patch series, not as a verdict on a whole approach.

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Thomas Kuhn
finding: Kuhn: normal science ignores or explains away anomalies; only an accumulation of troublesome anomalies yields crisis. Popper: a single reproducible anomaly can suffice. Lakatos sits between: anomalies tolerated while the belt is progressive.
numbers: Kuhn's five theory-choice criteria: accuracy, consistency, scope, simplicity, fruitfulness.
limits: Entry does not compare Kuhn and Lakatos directly.
agent_relevance: Three stop policies: one failure (Popper), anomaly accumulation (Kuhn), progress rate (Lakatos). Our detector uses the third.

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Pierre Duhem
finding: Duhem: hypotheses are tested in groups, so a failed prediction does not locate the error. Quine extended it to all statements (holism plus any statement can be kept true).
numbers: Quine attributes only holism to Duhem; Duhem's own claim is weaker (disconfirmation is ambiguous).
limits: No numbers; no Lakatos link on the page.
agent_relevance: Why a failed check must be traced to output before patching (G2).

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Karl Popper
finding: Popper held modifications are unscientific only when their sole purpose is to evade falsification. Lakatos's critique: falsification by conventionalist criteria does not show a theory false; high-level theories sit behind a protective belt.
numbers: Popper on psychoanalysis: no conceivable human behaviour which could contradict it.
limits: Page does not name sophisticated falsificationism.
agent_relevance: Ancestor of the patch-purpose test: ask whether a patch only evades the failure or also extends reach.

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Paul Feyerabend
finding: Feyerabend and Lakatos were to co-author For and Against Method; Feyerabend generalised from the limited validity of falsificationism to anything goes. Lakatos died in 1974 before replying.
numbers: Chronology entries: 1967, 1970, 1974.
limits: Tenacity and proliferation principles were not in the portion read.
agent_relevance: Pluralism and tenacity both have value; the guardrail concerns the cost of tenacity, not a ban.

source: Is artificial intelligence a degenerating program? A review of Hubert Dreyfus, What Computers Still Can't Do (Artificial Intelligence, 1996)
finding: Metadata only: applies the degenerating-programme label to symbolic AI. Full text could not be opened (403/redirect).
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Not opened; cite only for existence.
agent_relevance: Candidate for angle B: earliest Lakatosian reading of AI.

source: Nunan (1982) An immanent criticism of Lakatos' account of the degenerating phase of Bohr's atomic theory
finding: Metadata only: a published critique of Lakatos's own Bohr case.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Not opened (paywall).
agent_relevance: Test case for whether a degenerating label survives scrutiny; follow in angle B.

source: Is human sociobiology a progressive or a degenerating research programme? (BBS 1987)
finding: Metadata only: an applied use of the label in a behavioural science.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Not opened (paywall).
agent_relevance: Applying MSRP outside physics; follow in angle B.

source: Lakatos 'MSRP' overview by Sfetcu (2019), archive.org
finding: Secondary summary repeating Lakatos's claim that great achievements are 'a powerful problem-solving machinery' and that sophisticated falsificationism appraises a series of theories, not one.
numbers: Page cites: MSRP pp. 4, 38, 110, 114.
limits: Secondary and partly translated; use only to cross-check the primary.
